title: Same Tree
statement:
Given the roots of two binary trees p and q, write a function to check if they are the same or not.

Two binary trees are considered the same if they are structurally identical, and the nodes have the same value.
inputFormat:
Line 1: space-separated level-order string for tree p.
Line 2: space-separated level-order string for tree q.
(If a tree is empty, the line will be completely empty).
outputFormat: Print `YES` if they are the same, `NO` otherwise.
constraints:
0 <= The number of nodes in both trees <= 100
-10^4 <= Node.val <= 10^4

examples.explanation: Structurally different, even though same values.

starterCode.python:
import sys
lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
p = lines[0].split() if len(lines) > 0 else []
q = lines[1].split() if len(lines) > 1 else []
# Implement same tree logic
